LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: FRIENDLY LETTER

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter, part of Strand 8 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we write friendly letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy writing friendly letters for communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension,

   Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression,

   Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy writing friendly letters for communication.

   Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work collaboratively to collect samples of friendly letters from print and non-print sources,

2. identify components of a friendly letter,

3. discuss with peers the various components from the sample friendly letters,

4. compose a friendly letter related to the theme,

5. team up with peers to type the friendly letter on a digital device,

6. proofread their friendly letters and make corrections,

7. organise the friendly letters in their portfolio.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work collaboratively to collect samples of friendly letters from print and non-print sources,
2. identify components of a friendly letter,
3. discuss with peers the various components from the sample friendly letters,
4. compose a friendly letter related to the theme,
5. team up with peers to type the friendly letter on a digital device,
6. proofread their friendly letters and make corrections,
7. organise the friendly letters in their portfolio.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology to type the friendly letter on a digital device.

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner builds on their own learning experience when composing a friendly

letter related to the theme.

48

Values:
• Responsibility: This is nurtured as the learner exhibits accountability to accept input when proofreading their friendly letters

and making corrections.

• Patriotism: This is promoted as the learner is devoted to work with peers to read and share friendly letters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner works with peers to accomplish tasks and learn from each other.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of writing friendly letters to their learning of similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.

1. identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension,
2. write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression,
3. enjoy writing friendly letters for communication.

Remember the key question: Why do we write friendly letters?
